newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Meister says cybermoney is risk to policy.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Meister says cybermoney is risk to policy.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Edgar Meister said on Thursday that new payment systems like prepaid-cards and so-called cybermoney will make it harder for central banks to conduct monetary policy.

In a speech to the annual general meeting of the Federal Union of German Money and Valuables Transport Companies, Meister said that money supply in cash created a refinancing dependency of the private banks on the central bank.
This dependency was the lever for the central bank which allows it to influence market interest rates and indirectly the economy as well.
But card-money and internet-payment systems would replace the central bank as the issuer of money and thus weaken its influence on the money supply flow.
In the speech, made available in Frankfurt, Meister argued that the issue of electronic money should therefore be handled by banks exclusively.
They were the institutions best suited to ensure security and functionality of the payment systems, Meister contended.

"Not only do they have experience in handling payments systems but they are also subject to continuous surveillance with regards to credit worthiness and liquidity and have, on top of that, a liquidity reserve with the central bank."
Meister also suggested that as a measure of last resort the issue of electronic money could become a monopoly with the central bank - similar to the current practice with cash bills.
"This needs to be considered, if the necessary security can't be provided by private institutions," Meister said.
Complete security is not possible, however, Meister admitted, and called for systems that are able to detect fraud as soon as possible.
The introduction of the euro could foster the use of electronic money, he said.
"Specifically, the fact that at the start of the single currency on January 1, 1999 there will be no Euro-cash available yet, could boost electronic-payment systems," Meister believes.
